prompt: A reduction gives Hamiltonian-cycle graph edges cheap TSP weights and non-edges large penalties. What must the penalty ensure to rule out a proposed constant-factor approximation?

options.text: Every non-edge is merely more expensive than an edge
options.explanation: A small penalty may still lie inside the allowed approximation range.

options.text: The average no-case tour is expensive
options.explanation: The guarantee must separate every feasible no-case tour, including the cheapest.

options.text: Every no-case tour costs more than the approximation may return in the yes-case
options.explanation: Then checking the approximate output’s cost distinguishes Hamiltonian from non-Hamiltonian inputs.

options.text: The new distances satisfy the triangle inequality
options.explanation: The argument exploits arbitrary non-metric weights; metric TSP has constant-factor approximations.

workedExample: In the yes-case a tour uses only cheap graph edges, so the approximation must return within its promised factor of that cost. In the no-case every tour must use an expensive non-edge. Choose its penalty so that even the cheapest no-case tour lies beyond the whole allowed yes-case range. Only this separated gap lets the approximate cost decide Hamiltonian cycle.
